title: Exploring the shell structure of trapped superfluid gases
authors: G. Palkanoglou, R. Curry, S. Gandolfi
abstract: We provide quantum Monte Carlo calculations of a two-component Fermi system interacting with an attractive interaction confined in harmonic traps. We investigate the role of the interaction's scattering length and effective range and show its important role in modifying shell effects in the structure of these systems. We show that in the strongly interacting regime, where the scattering length is large, the dominant role to shell effects is due to the effective range. These conclusions are very relevant for nuclear physics, in particular for neutron-rich systems, and open the way to perform new atomic experiments that can help to explain the disappearance of shell-effects in nuclei.
summary: The paper uses Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study trapped superfluid Fermi gases, examining how their shell structure changes as the interaction strength approaches unitarity. The key finding is that strong pairing correlations effectively wash out the characteristic shell gaps observed at weaker interactions. This provides a theoretical model relevant for understanding nuclear physics phenomena in exotic neutron-rich isotopes.
main_problem: The study investigates how shell structure, a characteristic feature of quantum systems, evolves when superfluid Fermi gases are tuned towards the unitary limit.
main_result: Shell effects are observed at finite interaction strengths but demonstrably vanish as the system approaches unitarity, suggesting strong pairing correlations suppress single-particle behavior.
method: The research employs Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods, specifically Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC), alongside Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) calculations to determine ground state energies and gaps.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a two-component Fermi gas confined in a harmonic trap. The interactions are characterized by tunable scattering length ($a$) and effective range ($r_e$), allowing exploration across different interaction regimes, including the unitary limit.
key_observables: Two-particle separation energies ($S_{2N}$), two-particle shell gaps ($\Delta_{2N}$), and Odd-Even Staggering (OES) quantifying pairing correlations.
important_parameters: Scattering length ($a$), effective range ($r_e$), particle number ($N$), and the unitary limit ($a 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a harmonic trap potential, which differs from the finite-depth potentials found in real nuclei; furthermore, discrepancies exist between calculated pairing gap scaling parameters ($\eta$) and experimental values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how energy gaps and separation energies diminish towards unitarity as interaction parameters are varied, confirming the suppression of shell structure by strong correlations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using QMC for trapped Fermi gases. It then systematically analyzes observables like $S_{2N}$ and $\Delta_{2N}$ across varying interaction strengths to demonstrate the vanishing of shell effects at unitarity, linking this mechanism to pairing correlations.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges cold atomic physics (ultracold Fermi gases) with fundamental nuclear structure questions (shell evolution in neutron-rich nuclei), providing a clean quantum simulation platform for understanding complex many-body phenomena like pairing and correlation effects.
